name: Air Fryer Crispy Salmon Sandwiches with Lemon-Caper Mayo

components.name: Crispy Salmon

ingredients.name: Raw skinless salmon, four equal 170 g portions
Seasoned panko breadcrumbs, including expected leftover
Raw egg whites, measured without shell

steps: Pat salmon dry and divide into four pieces. Place measured egg white in a shallow bowl and panko in another. Season fish lightly with salt.
Dip fish in egg white, then press into panko; shake off excess breadcrumbs, noting the unused amount for final nutrition recalculation.
Lightly spray with oil and air fry at 200 C for about 8-12 minutes, turning once, until crust is golden and fish reaches 63 C.
For batch prep, store cooked breaded salmon separately from buns, mayonnaise and raw greens; re-crisp fish in air fryer and assemble when eating.

components.name: Bun, Salad & Slaw

ingredients.name: Raw shredded cabbage for crunchy side slaw

steps: Mix shredded cabbage with lemon just before serving. Prepare bread buns with lettuce and tomatoes, then add one cooked breaded salmon piece and a quarter of caper mayo to each.

components.name: Lemon-Caper Mayo
steps: Mix light mayonnaise, chopped capers and lemon into a sauce; refrigerate until ready to assemble sandwiches.

notes: Draft — needs Mirna review: not kitchen-tested yet; macros and cooked yields are estimates.

Skinnytaste lemon-caper salmon sandwich; added tomato and cabbage side and increased salmon raw weight for complete-meal recipe. Unused panko and egg white mean nutrition may overestimate coating eaten.
Planning: AIR FRYER ONLY for main, toast buns optional.
Freezer: breaded salmon may freeze but loses crispness; buns can freeze alone; salad and mayo fresh
Dietary: Fish, egg, wheat; mayonnaise contains egg.

Refrigerate within 2 hours (1 hour above 32°C) in shallow containers at 4°C or colder, for 3–4 days at most, and follow the shorter seafood limit above. Cook fish and shellfish to 63°C and reheat leftovers to at least 74°C.

preservationAndReheating: Refrigerate cooked food promptly in shallow covered containers. Target within 2 hours, or 1 hour when ambient temperature exceeds 32 C.
Refrigerate at 4 C or below for 3-4 days maximum; for many fish and shrimp dishes, prioritize eating within 1-2 days for quality and freeze later-week cooked portions promptly.

Cook fish and crustaceans to 63 C (145 F) or applicable local food-safety standard, and reheat cooked leftovers to 74 C. For crab cakes containing egg binder and purchased cooked crab, reheat to 74 C.
When recipe includes rice, cool rapidly and refrigerate promptly; do not leave cooked rice at room temperature.
Freeze in suitable airtight food-safe containers. Defrost in refrigerator, not on counter. Re-crisp breading in an air fryer when possible.
Do not freeze fresh avocado, uncooked tomato/cucumber/cabbage salad, or mayonnaise/yogurt-based dressing unless kitchen-tested separately.
Freezer suitability here describes expected eating quality, not laboratory validated shelf life.
